News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: Capital goods, strategic manufacturing sectors to generate 50 lakh jobs over next five years: CGSSC
item.description: The Capital Goods & Strategic Skill Council emphasized the projected creation of 50 lakh job opportunities in India. These jobs will primarily be in capital goods and strategic manufacturing sectors over the next five years. There is a significant demand for skilled workers in various technical roles such as riggers and CNC operators. Advanced manufacturing and automation training are crucial to meet this demand effectively.

item.title: India to cross $1 trillion export mark by March 2027 despite proposed 25% US tariff: ASSOCHAM Secretary General
item.description: Speaking to on the sidelines of ASSOCHAM's India Energy Sovereignty Summit 2026, ASSOCHAM Secretary General Saurabh Sanyal expressed confidence in India's export performance, highlighting that the country's exports have already crossed USD 500 billion and are growing at a rate of 15 per cent.

item.title: Even 17% tariff under India-US trade deal may offer little competitive advantage to Indian exporters: FIEO
item.description: Ajay Sahai from the Federation of Indian Export Organisations expressed concerns about a potential BTA with the US. He mentioned that even a 17 per cent tariff concession may not give Indian exporters an advantage. Competing nations, particularly in Southeast Asia, could secure better trade terms through their own agreements. Sahai estimated an 8 per cent additional cost burden for exporters if US tariffs rise to 25 per cent.

item.title: Nitin Gadkari announces Rs 1 lakh crore road projects for Bengal, promises 250-km Kolkata ring road
item.description: Declaring that the Centre would back Bengal's infrastructure push with all necessary financial resources, Gadkari said projects worth around Rs 40,000 crore had already been completed in the state, while works worth Rs 35,000 crore, covering approximately 450 km, were under implementation.

item.title: India attracts $31 bn in climate equity funding, but $22-24 trn needed by 2070: BCG-IVCA
item.description: India has secured nearly USD 31 billion in climate funding since 2021, focusing primarily on power and transport. Underfunded sectors such as manufacturing, waste management, and agriculture require significant investment to meet future goals. The country needs approximately USD 22 trillion in total investment by 2070 to support climate transition. Improving investment viability through innovative financing structures has been identified as a crucial step.

item.title: Govt projects Kharif foodgrain production at 167.14 mln tonnes despite El Nino; 2025-26 crop output a record
item.description: Kharif foodgrain production for the 2026-27 crop year is projected at 167.14 million tonnes amid weather challenges. Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced these estimates despite El Nino and a delayed monsoon. In the previous crop year, foodgrain production reached a record high of 378.54 million tonnes. Additionally, pulses and oilseeds are being prioritized due to India's reliance on imports.

item.title: How Donald Trump's proposed fresh tariff salvo for India compare with rival nations
item.description: The US has proposed a 25% tariff on Indian imports to address excess industrial capacity issues. This rate could decrease to 17% if a trade deal is reached. India's trade ministry is reviewing the US's trade practices allegations while defending its own situation. Trade talks have been prolonged due to various complications, including tariff laws and military incidents.

item.title: US tariff threat: Indian traders urge Modi to hit back with 25% duty
item.description: The Chamber of Trading Industry (CTI) has urged the government to consider imposing a 25 per cent retaliatory tariff on US goods if Washington proceeds with higher duties on Indian products, warning that the proposed measures could affect exports worth USD 48 billion and put around five lakh jobs at risk.

item.title: USTR proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including 25% on India; Indian experts react
From ropeways to ring roads: Karan Adani reveals the group’s next big bets at ET Bengal Ascends
item.description: Adani Group aims to expand its operations in West Bengal by bidding for thermal power and infrastructure projects. The group plans to develop the Kolkata Outer Ring Road to ease urban congestion. Karan Adani highlighted the importance of strategic infrastructure planning to avoid bottlenecks in port operations. The company secured a renewable power supply contract for 1,750 MW starting July 2028.

item.title: US accuses India of creating manufacturing overcapacity through PLI, Make in India schemes
item.description: Concerns have emerged from the US about India’s industrial approaches, especially those facilitating manufacturing growth and export enhancement. Initiatives like Make in India, coupled with financial policies that uphold low interest rates, are under scrutiny. The US Trade Representative details factors tied to excess capacity in Indian manufacturing, pointing to issues in specific industries like steel and solar energy, which pose notable challenges for US companies and employees.

item.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, Rs 5,548 crore for Narmada-Tapi project
item.description: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi Valley Diversion Project and a draft bill to regulate private aided schools, among 14 decisions taken at the meeting.

item.title: India-UK investment treaty talks stall, pact unlikely soon, officials say
item.description: The prospect of India pursuing a bilateral investment treaty with the UK appears grim, primarily because of enduring disputes related to taxation and arbitration. Talks have hit a snag, with both countries entrenched in contrasting views on investor protection and sovereignty. Future discussions will divert from the investment treaty, concentrating on economic dialogues instead.

item.title: Net FDI turns negative at USD 4.95 billion in Sep on flow moderation, higher outflows: RBI
item.description: The month of September 2026 marked a decline in net foreign direct investment in India, reaching negative USD 4.95 billion, primarily due to decreasing gross inflows and more substantial foreign investment repatriations. In contrast, outward direct investment from India rose to USD 4.41 billion. Although foreign portfolio investments faced a drop of USD 6.652 billion in October, they bounced back in November, achieving USD 12.

item.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman chairs 12th pre-Budget consultation with education, skilling and sports stakeholders
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday held the 12th pre-Budget consultation with stakeholders from schooling, vocational education, skilling and sports sectors ahead of the Union Budget 2027-28. Senior officials from key ministries and the Chief Economic Adviser attended the meeting as the government continued gathering sector-specific inputs for budget formulation.

item.title: India's sugar output seen falling to decade low, says industry body
item.description: India's sugar production is expected to fall to a decade low of 26.52 million metric tons in the 2026/27 season, down from 27.97 million tons a year earlier, as lower rainfall is likely to hurt sugar cane yields in key growing states, the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association said.

item.title: RBI hunts for possible '$2 million loophole' in importers' forex transactions
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped up scrutiny of importers' forex transactions amid concerns that companies may be splitting deals below the $2 million threshold to avoid additional reserve requirements. The move follows a sharp fall in average dollar-buying transaction sizes since October 10, even as the number of deals has risen, prompting fresh compliance checks on banks.

item.title: Poultry body seeks stock limits on maize, soyabean; warns of Rs 40-50/kg rise in chicken price
item.description: The All India Poultry Breeders Association is urging the government to impose stock limits on maize and soyabean. Rising feed prices have caused significant distress for poultry farmers amid claims of artificial scarcity. Many poultry farms are shutting down as production costs exceed earnings from chicken sales. The association estimates that chicken prices could increase significantly if conditions do not improve soon.

item.title: India allocates 8,606 tonnes of raw cane sugar for export to US under Tariff Rate Quota scheme
item.description: India has allocated 8,606 metric tonnes of raw cane sugar for export to the US under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme for the 2027 US fiscal year, running from October 1, 2026, to September 30, 2027. The scheme allows shipments at zero or concessional import duty.

item.title: India and Netherlands looking at boosting cooperation in clean energy, shipbuilding: MEA
item.description: India and the Netherlands are enhancing cooperation in several sectors including shipping and green hydrogen. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Dutch counterpart Tom Berendsen met to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. They reviewed ongoing engagements across areas such as trade, technology, and maritime development. Both sides emphasized the significance of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement for economic growth.

item.title: India's economic activity growth hits four-year high of 9% in October: Jefferies
item.description: India's economic activity growth hit a four-year high of 9% year-on-year in October. The increase was largely attributed to strong industrial activity and a delayed festive season. However, rural demand indicators remained weak due to a subdued monsoon. While bank credit growth reached a nearly 12-year high, inflationary pressures intensified simultaneously. Overall, the report highlights a mixed outlook for future economic activity amidst varying consumer behaviors.

item.title: India, Canada 'very close' to conclude trade pact negotiations: Official
item.description: Negotiators from India and Canada are engaging daily to finalize the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement negotiations. A sixth round of discussions took place recently, focusing on key areas such as trade and investment. Both countries aim to increase bilateral trade to USD 50 billion by 2030, after a decline in trade values. India is also working on a separate bilateral investment protection agreement with Canada.

item.title: India-EU free trade pact to open new opportunities for trade, investment: German state leader
item.description: India and the European Union concluded negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement that is set to be finalized soon. Minister-President Olaf Lies of Lower Saxony emphasized the potential benefits for both Indian and German businesses. He mentioned cooperation in areas like digitalization and artificial intelligence as key prospects for collaboration. The partnership aims to enhance skilled workforce mobility with training programs for young Indians.

item.title: India, UK working to resolve technical glitch over Scotch whisky duty concessions under trade pact
item.description: The Commerce Ministry is working with the Finance Ministry, importers and UK authorities to resolve a customs classification issue affecting duty concessions on Scotch whisky imports under the India-UK trade pact. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said India remains committed to its tariff obligations and has urged the DRI to release pending consignments.

item.title: RBI Governor asks NBFCs, housing finance firms to bolster cyber defences
item.description: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra called on non-banking finance companies and housing finance companies to bolster cybersecurity measures. He emphasized the importance of a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber threats. Malhotra also highlighted the necessity for responsible credit growth and customer prioritization within these financial institutions. Participants exchanged feedback on policy and operational aspects affecting the NBFC sector during the meeting.

item.title: Deepak Parekh flags missing housing starts data in India's economic indicators
item.description: Deepak Parekh addressed the Data Users Conference highlighting the lack of official housing start data in India. He emphasized that this data is crucial due to strong linkages with many allied industries. Parekh noted the recent revision of the GDP base year to 2022-23 and its implications for economic indicators. He also mentioned the importance of high-frequency indicators in assessing economic trends beyond quarterly GDP figures.

item.title: India weighs 20% export duty on select rice varieties to boost domestic supply
item.description: India is contemplating the imposition of export duties on specific rice varieties to improve domestic supplies. This measure aims to mitigate rising prices faced by consumers and industries in the local market. Although the export duty might slow rice exports, it is unlikely to halt shipments completely due to competitive pricing. The poultry and cattle feed sectors have been notably affected by the surge in broken rice prices.

item.title: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman holds 11th pre-Budget consultation with R&D, education experts
item.description: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 11th pre-Budget consultation focused on research and education. This meeting was part of the preparations for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28. Notably, significant allocations were made in the previous Budget for research, innovation and higher education. Earlier, another meeting was held with health and social sector experts for the same purpose.

item.title: Insolvency framework should be responsive to dynamic needs of economy: Official
item.description: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code reforms are underway, emphasizing the need for responsiveness to economic dynamics. Corporate Affairs Secretary Pallavi Jain Govil stressed the importance of promptly implementing approved insolvency resolution plans. Creditors have recovered Rs 4.30 lakh crore through these plans, highlighting their effectiveness. IBBI officials noted that litigation significantly contributes to delays in the resolution process.

item.title: Ramayan Circuit boost: Modi, Balen Shah flag off Ayodhya-Janakpur train, Ram-Sita birthplaces linked
Budget 2027: FM Sitharaman holds 10th pre-Budget meeting with health, social sector stakeholders
item.description: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the tenth pre-Budget consultation with health and social sector stakeholders. This consultation is a significant step in preparing for the Union Budget 2027-28. Prior meetings have included various sectors, covering agriculture, manufacturing, and health. The government allocated more funds to healthcare in the previous budget, marking a 10 percent increase.

item.title: India to be one of APAC champions with 7% GDP forecast for FY27, but El Nino will prove costly: S&P
item.description: S&P Global Ratings projects a robust 7 percent GDP growth for India in the current and upcoming fiscal years. However, the impact of El Nino is anticipated to drive food prices higher, thus increasing inflationary pressures. With input costs on the rise, these expenses are likely to be transferred to consumers.

item.title: India factory demand offsets weaker services growth in November, PMI shows
item.description: India's private sector activity experienced marginal growth in November, driven by manufacturing demand and production. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose slightly from October, indicating continued expansion. The manufacturing sector achieved a nine-month high, while the services sector saw a decline in growth. Employment trends diverged, with factories increasing hiring and services sectors reducing jobs. Companies exhibited optimism about future performance, although confidence remained below historic averages.

item.title: The decade India turned the tide on poverty
item.description: The World Bank report highlights that nearly 50 crore Indians have moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023. Government efforts include health initiatives and direct benefit transfers that empower households. Women's participation in self-help groups has transformed economic opportunities for many. Continued investment in infrastructure aims to support future growth and prevent slippage back into poverty. Achieving Viksit Bharat by 2047 remains a shared goal for India's development.

item.title: India-EU trade deal likely to be signed on December 16
item.description: Described as the 'mother of all deals', the FTA will provide duty-free access to the EU for 93% of India's exports, while making imports of luxury cars and wines from the bloc cheaper. Together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and about one-third of international trade, valued at $11 trillion of the $33 trillion global trade market.

item.title: Asia, Africa to drive expansion of India's export markets as shipments grow across regions
item.description: India's merchandise exports have shown strong growth, particularly in Africa and Asia, according to recent government data. Exports to Africa increased by 44 percent, while shipments to Asia surpassed USD 100 billion. Engineering goods, electronic goods, and petroleum products have driven this expansion significantly. Notable growth was observed in markets such as Tanzania and Kenya in Africa.

item.title: Rising government debt unlikely to trigger broad sovereign crisis in 2027: UBS
item.description: Government borrowing and debt-servicing costs are likely to escalate challenges for major economies by 2027. UBS reports that pressure stems from refinanced debt from low interest rates previously. Factors contributing to public finance pressure include ageing populations and entitlement spending. Measures like bond buybacks and changes in debt issuance strategies can help manage financing pressures. Nonetheless, UBS warns about potential difficulties that could lead to a debt crisis.

item.title: Government, corporate spending to sustain global growth in 2027 as inflation eases: JPMorgan
item.description: Global economic growth is projected to be resilient in 2027 due to continued government investment and corporate spending. Investment in technology and recovery in consumer demand are expected to drive this growth forward. Corporate investment, especially in artificial intelligence, is noteworthy, with major firms planning significant expenditure. Inflation pressures are anticipated to ease, strengthening household spending. However, rising government borrowing and competition for capital may pose challenges for financial markets.

item.title: GST Network adds metro rail as fifth mode of transport in e-way bill system
item.description: GSTN has introduced metro rail as a new mode of transport in the e-way bill system. This addition follows a government notification released on October 26, enhancing transport options for users. The e-way bill system now includes five modes: Road, Rail, Air, Ship, and Metro Rail. Users must select metro rail and enter transport document numbers for transactions.

item.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy
item.description: India and Finland are working to strengthen their economic relationship by focusing on startup collaboration. Finnish Ambassador Mikko Kivikoski stated the importance of engaging with Indian startups for promoting investment. The Polar Bear Pitching event showcased startups, with Yash Goliya winning to compete globally in 2027. Bilateral trade between the nations is growing, with significant increases in recent years.

item.title: Nirmala Sitharaman chairs ninth pre-Budget consultation with housing, urbanisation and culture stakeholders
item.description: The consultation was held "with the experts and stakeholders from the housing, urbanisation, and culture sectors in connection with the Union Budget 2027-28", the Finance Ministry said in a post on X. The secretaries of the Department of Economic Affairs and the Department of Urban Development attended the meeting. The ministry's post gave no details of the proposals made by participants.

item.title: No FAST-DS declaration needed for foreign bank a/c up to Rs 20 lakh with disclosed funds: I-T dept
item.description: The Income Tax Department has announced exemptions for individuals with foreign bank accounts under FAST-DS. Individuals with balances up to Rs 20 lakh from disclosed sources do not need to file declarations. This exemption applies as long as the accounts contain no undisclosed income or unaccounted deposits. The scheme provides a one-time opportunity to disclose foreign assets and income by December 31.

item.title: Union Minister Chouhan unveils country's first indigenous H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu
item.description: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan introduced the first indigenous H5N1 vaccine for chickens developed in India. This significant vaccine was created by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases located in Bhopal. Officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry highlighted the importance of this vaccine against the pathogenic avian influenza virus. The event was attended by notable figures including Madhya Pradesh Sports and Youth Welfare Minister Vishwas Sarang.

item.title: RBI expected to raise rates in December, deliver final hike in February: Report
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to raise its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and take it to 6% in February as inflation breaches its 6% tolerance limit, a Reuters poll showed. Rising energy costs and uneven monsoon rainfall have intensified inflationary pressures.

item.title: India's capital goods market could reach $1.2 trillion by 2047, driven by data centres, chips: Report
item.description: India's capital goods market could expand to USD 1-1.2 trillion by 2047, driven by rising investments in data centres, semiconductors, defence and clean energy, a CII-BCG report said. Annual capital expenditure across major industries is projected to rise 30% to Rs 32 lakh crore by FY27-29.

item.title: FM Sitharaman holds eighth pre-Budget consultation with labour, employment sector stakeholders
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the eighth pre-Budget consultation with employment and labour sector stakeholders on Friday, seeking inputs for the Union Budget 2027-28. The meeting follows consultations with infrastructure, energy, IT, banking and other sectors as the government prepares its annual Budget, scheduled to be presented on February 1, 2027.

item.title: India's wheat area set for steepest decline in 26 years as farmers switch crops
item.description: India is experiencing its most severe decline in wheat acreage in 26 years due to insufficient monsoon rains. Farmers are shifting to less water-intensive crops like chickpeas and rapeseed, which promise better returns. The government's minimal increase in wheat procurement prices has also discouraged wheat planting among farmers. As a result, wheat acreage is expected to drop to its lowest level in four years.

item.title: India, Japan deepen defence, tech, and economic security ties as EAM Jaishankar concludes Tokyo visit
item.description: During the visit, Jaishankar participated in the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue (2+2) alongside Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and their Japanese counterparts, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.

item.title: Customs should review classification of bulk Scotch whisky imports: GTRI
item.description: Customs authorities are facing a tariff dispute regarding bulk Scotch whisky imports following the India-UK trade agreement. The classification issue revolves around whether Scotch falls under specific tariff codes for spirits or food preparations. Importers currently classify bulk Scotch under a code that entitles them to reduced duties. Recent changes have led to customs reclassifying these imports, which doubles the duty rate significantly.

item.title: Piyush Goyal calls for trusted India-US supply chains, deeper economic cooperation
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal urged India and the US to build trusted supply chains for better collaboration. He highlighted that India's strengths in talent and manufacturing complement America's capital and technology. The minister also encouraged increased partnerships between educational institutions in both nations. Goyal expressed optimism for achieving USD one trillion in exports during the current fiscal year.
